text:
Three masses $M=100\mathrm{kg},\mathrm{m}_{1}=10\mathrm{kg}$ and $\mathrm{m}_{2}=20\mathrm{kg}$ are arranged in a system as shown in figure. All the surfaces are frictionless and strings are inextensible and weightless. The pulleys are also weightless and frictionless. A force $\mathrm{F}$ is applied on the system so that the mass $\mathrm{m}_{2}$ moves upward with an acceleration of $2\mathrm{ms}^{-2}$. The value of $\mathrm{F}$ is :

( Take $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{ms}^{-2}$ )


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Denote by $a$ the acceleration of $M$ to the right. As $M$ accelerates, the hanging block $m_{2}$ is pressed against the right face of $M$, so $m_{2}$ moves horizontally with $M$ (acceleration $a$) while rising at $2\text{m s}^{-2}$. The string is inextensible, so $m_{1}$ slides away from the pulley, to the left relative to $M$, at $2\text{m s}^{-2}$; its acceleration relative to the ground is $(a-2)$ to the right.


[IMG]

Vertical motion of $m_{2}$:

$T-m_{2}g=m_{2}(2)\Rightarrow T=20(10+2)=240\text{N}$

The only horizontal force on $m_{1}$ is the tension, towards the pulley:

$T=m_{1}(a-2)\Rightarrow 240=10(a-2)\Rightarrow a=26\text{m s}^{-2}$

For the whole system ($M$, pulley, $m_{1}$, $m_{2}$) the floor is frictionless, so $F$ is the only external horizontal force:

$F=Ma+m_{1}(a-2)+m_{2}a=100(26)+10(24)+20(26)=2600+240+520=3360\text{N}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift

text: Two projectiles thrown at $30^{\circ }$ and $45^{\circ }$ with the horizontal respectively, reach the maximum height in same time. The ratio of their initial velocities is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve this problem, we need to understand the relationship between the angles of projection, the initial velocities, and the time taken to reach maximum height for each projectile.

The formula to calculate the time to reach the maximum height is given by:

$t=\frac{u\sin θ}{g}$

where:

$t$ is the time to reach maximum height,

$u$ is the initial velocity,

$θ$ is the angle of projection, and

$g$ is the acceleration due to gravity.

Given that the projectiles reach the maximum height in the same time, we can set up the following equation:

$\frac{u_{1}\sin 30^{\circ }}{g}=\frac{u_{2}\sin 45^{\circ }}{g}$

Since $\sin 30^{\circ }=\frac{1}{2}$ and $\sin 45^{\circ }=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, the equation simplifies to:

$\frac{u_{1}\cdot \frac{1}{2}}{g}=\frac{u_{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}{g}$

Canceling out the common terms (i.e., $g$ and $\frac{1}{2}$), we get:

$u_{1}=u_{2}\sqrt{2}$

Hence, the ratio of their initial velocities is:

$\frac{u_{1}}{u_{2}}=\sqrt{2}$

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C: $\sqrt{2}:1$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift

text: If the initial velocity in horizontal direction of a projectile is unit vector $\hat{i}$ and the equation of trajectory is $y=5x(1-x)$. The $y$ component vector of the initial velocity is $______________$ $\hat{j}$. ($\mathrm{Take}$ $\left. \mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}\right )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
If the initial velocity in the horizontal direction of a projectile is represented by the unit vector $\hat{i}$ and the equation of the trajectory is given by $y=5x(1-x)$, we need to find the $y$ component vector of the initial velocity. (Given: $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$)

The trajectory equation can be expanded as:

$y=5x-5x^{2}$

In the general form of a projectile's trajectory: $y=x\tan θ-\frac{1}{2}\frac{gx^{2}}{v_{0}^{2}}$

Here, the equation compares as follows:

$\tan θ=5=\frac{u_{y}}{u_{x}}$

Given that the initial horizontal velocity component, $u_{x}$, is 1 (unit vector $\hat{i}$), we can find $u_{y}$ from the relationship:

$u_{y}=5\times 1=5$

Therefore, the $y$ component vector of the initial velocity is 5$\hat{j}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift

text:
The effective current I in the given circuit at very high frequencies will be $___________ A$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At very high frequency the inductive reactance $X_{L}=ωL\to \infty$, so each inductor acts as an open circuit, while the capacitive reactance $X_{C}=\dfrac{1}{ωC}\to 0$, so each capacitor acts as a plain connecting wire.

The $20\text{mH}$ and $50\text{mH}$ inductors lie at the two ends of the top wire, so no current flows through the top-left and top-right $8\Omega$ resistors. The two vertical $0.5μ\text{F}$ capacitors join the upper junctions to the lower ones, so the top $4\Omega$ (with $6μ\text{F}$) and the lower middle $4\Omega$ (with $0.8μ\text{F}$) are connected between the same two points, in parallel. The lower-left $1\Omega$ and the lower-right $2\Omega$ are in series with this pair.


[IMG]

$R_{\text{eq}}=1+\dfrac{4\times 4}{4+4}+2=5\Omega$

$I=\dfrac{V}{R_{\text{eq}}}=\dfrac{220}{5}=44\text{A}$

Hence, the answer is 44.

text: In the hydrogen spectrum, $λ$ be the wavelength of first transition line of Lyman series. The wavelength difference will be "a$λ$'' between the wavelength of $3^{\text{rd}}$ transition line of Paschen series and that of $2^{\text{nd}}$ transition line of Balmer series where $\mathrm{a}=$ $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With $\dfrac{1}{λ}=R\left (\dfrac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\dfrac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right )$:

First Lyman line ($2\to 1$): $\dfrac{1}{λ}=R\left (1-\dfrac{1}{4}\right )=\dfrac{3R}{4}\Rightarrow λ=\dfrac{4}{3R}$.

Third Paschen line ($6\to 3$): $\dfrac{1}{λ_{P}}=R\left (\dfrac{1}{9}-\dfrac{1}{36}\right )=\dfrac{R}{12}\Rightarrow λ_{P}=\dfrac{12}{R}$.

Second Balmer line ($4\to 2$): $\dfrac{1}{λ_{B}}=R\left (\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{16}\right )=\dfrac{3R}{16}\Rightarrow λ_{B}=\dfrac{16}{3R}$.

$λ_{P}-λ_{B}=\dfrac{12}{R}-\dfrac{16}{3R}=\dfrac{20}{3R}=5\times \dfrac{4}{3R}=5λ$

Hence, the answer is 5.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Morning Shift
